Wa'il broke his leg in a football match, and he had to stay in hospital for weeks.

Muhannad sat next to him in class. Now Wa'il's seat was empty, and the class was quiet without his laugh.

Muhannad said to his mother, "I want to visit Wa'il, but I don't know what to say to him."

She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The deed most loved by Allah is joy that you bring to a Muslim.' So think: what would make him happy?"

Muhannad thought for a long time. Wa'il loves football, he loves laughing, and he loves the class team.

So at break time he gathered the boys in the class and said, "I've got an idea."

The boys made a big poster. Each of them drew himself on it and wrote Wa'il a short message.

In the middle of the poster they drew a goal with a ball in it, and under it: "We're waiting for you, goalie!"

Then they collected some of their pocket money and bought a new football, and each of them wrote his name on it.

And Muhannad said, "I'll bring him our lessons every day, so he doesn't fall behind."
They went to the hospital with their teacher. When they came into the room, Wa'il lifted his head in surprise. Then he saw the poster and laughed so loudly that people in the corridor could hear.

Then they gave him the ball. He turned it over in his hands, reading the names one by one, and then hugged it to his chest.

He said, "I didn't think you'd remember me."

The nurse said to the teacher, "This is the first day he's eaten all his food since he came here."

And every day Muhannad brought him the lessons and told him what had happened in class, and they laughed together.

When Wa'il left the hospital and came back to class on crutches, all the boys stood up and clapped.

Wa'il said, "It wasn't just the medicine that made me better. What made me better was that you made me happy."

Afterwards, Muhannad would say, "I've never been as happy in my life as I was the day Wa'il laughed."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The deed most loved by Allah is joy that you bring to a Muslim."

📖 Narrated by At-Tabarani, and graded good (hasan) by the scholars of hadith. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
